UGen absdif ( UGen const &  leftOperand,
UGen const &  rightOperand 
) throw ()

Global function for the UGen::absdif() binary operator.

This makes: 

 UGen resultAbsDif  = SinOsc::AR(100, 0, 0.4).absdif(SinOsc::AR(400, 0, 0.3)); // creates a BinaryAbsDifUGen

..equivalent to: 

 UGen resultAbsDif  =  absdif(SinOsc::AR(100, 0, 0.4), SinOsc::AR(400, 0, 0.3)); // creates a BinaryAbsDifUGen
Parameters:
leftOperand The left-hand-side of the operator.
rightOperand The right-hand-side of the operator.
Returns:
The new UGen which is a result of the absdif() operation.

Buffer absdif ( const float  leftOperand,
Buffer const &  rightOperand 
) throw ()

Return a new Buffer with the binary operator applied to all channels.

The resulting Buffer will be the size of the rightOperand and have the same number of channels. The constant leftOperand will be applied to all channels and values using the absdif() function.

See also:
Buffer::absdif(Buffer const& rightOperand)

Definition at line 118 of file ugen_BinaryOpUGens.cpp.

Buffer absdif ( Buffer const &  leftOperand,
Buffer const &  rightOperand 
) throw ()

Return a new Buffer with the binary operator applied to all channels.

The resulting Buffer will be the size of the largest of the two input Buffers, the smaller Buffer will be effectively padded with zeroes. The resulting Buffer will have a number of channels equal to the highest number of channels in the two input Buffers. When applying the binary operator to two Buffers which have a different number of channels the smaller Buffer's channels will be accessed cyclically (i.e., using wrapped indices).

See also:
Buffer::absdif(Buffer const& rightOperand)

Buffer atan2 ( Buffer const &  leftOperand,
Buffer const &  rightOperand 
) throw ()

Return a new Buffer with the binary operator applied to all channels.

The resulting Buffer will be the size of the largest of the two input Buffers, the smaller Buffer will be effectively padded with zeroes. The resulting Buffer will have a number of channels equal to the highest number of channels in the two input Buffers. When applying the binary operator to two Buffers which have a different number of channels the smaller Buffer's channels will be accessed cyclically (i.e., using wrapped indices).

See also:
Buffer::atan2(Buffer const& rightOperand)

Buffer operator/ ( const float  leftOperand,
Buffer const &  rightOperand 
) throw ()

Return a new Buffer with the binary operator applied to all channels.

The resulting Buffer will be the size of the rightOperand and have the same number of channels. The constant leftOperand will be applied to all channels and values using the / operator. Like UGen, Buffer does some optimising if rightOperand is a single value and implments a multiplication instead (if this is possible and beneficial).

See also:
Buffer::operator/(Buffer const& rightOperand)

Definition at line 95 of file ugen_BinaryOpUGens.cpp.

Buffer pow ( Buffer const &  leftOperand,
Buffer const &  rightOperand 
) throw ()

Return a new Buffer with the binary operator applied to all channels.

The resulting Buffer will be the size of the largest of the two input Buffers, the smaller Buffer will be effectively padded with zeroes. The resulting Buffer will have a number of channels equal to the highest number of channels in the two input Buffers. When applying the binary operator to two Buffers which have a different number of channels the smaller Buffer's channels will be accessed cyclically (i.e., using wrapped indices).

See also:
Buffer::pow(Buffer const& rightOperand)

Buffer sqrsum ( Buffer const &  leftOperand,
Buffer const &  rightOperand 
) throw ()

Return a new Buffer with the binary operator applied to all channels.

The resulting Buffer will be the size of the largest of the two input Buffers, the smaller Buffer will be effectively padded with zeroes. The resulting Buffer will have a number of channels equal to the highest number of channels in the two input Buffers. When applying the binary operator to two Buffers which have a different number of channels the smaller Buffer's channels will be accessed cyclically (i.e., using wrapped indices).

See also:
Buffer::sqrsum(Buffer const& rightOperand)
